title: He saw him a second time.
subtitle: The second sighting, on the Night Journey
then: A'ishah reported that the Prophet ﷺ told her {idea}it was Jibril{/idea}, seen only twice in his real form. Ibn Kathir says this second time was {idea}during the Night of Isra{/idea}, the night journey.
now: You notice something once and wonder if you imagined it. You see it again, exactly the same, and your doubt is gone. {idea}A second witness of the same thing settles the matter.{/idea}
new: He saw the same angel, in the same true form, a second time.
try: Recall two separate times a prayer of yours was answered. Let them steady you today.

title: At the Lote Tree where everything stops.
subtitle: The boundary of the seventh heaven
then: Ibn Mas'ud described Sidrat al-Muntaha as {idea}in the seventh heaven{/idea}. There everything that rises from the earth ends and is held, and everything that comes down from above ends and is held. The Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril there.
now: Your deeds, your duas, the quiet good you did on a Tuesday. You never see where they go. {reward}This verse names a place where what rises from the earth arrives.{/reward} Nothing you send up just vanishes.
old: My small prayers disappear into nothing.
new: What rises from the earth reaches a known place and is held there.
try: Make one sincere dua today and trust that it is going somewhere.

title: Right beside it, the Garden of Refuge.
subtitle: Paradise placed next to the boundary
then: The vision is located precisely: the Lote Tree, and {reward}near it the Garden of Abode{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ was shown where Paradise lies. The listeners in Makkah were being told that the Garden is a real place, not a story.
now: You are tired of moving, of rent, of a hospital corridor, of never feeling settled. The word here is refuge, a place you come to rest. {reward}That home is real, and it has an address.{/reward}
old: Paradise is a nice idea, far and vague.
new: The Garden is a real place of refuge, shown and located.
try: When you feel unsettled today, say quietly: my real home is the Garden of Refuge.

title: Covered by what covered it.
subtitle: A sight too great to list
then: Ibn Kathir says angels, Allah's light and {reward}spectacular colors{/reward} covered the Tree. Ibn Mas'ud said golden butterflies. That night the Prophet ﷺ was given {reward}the five prayers{/reward}, the closing verses of al-Baqarah, and forgiveness of grave sins for those who do not associate partners with Allah.
now: You pray Maghrib in a rush between work and dinner. That prayer was a gift handed over at the highest place a human ever stood. {idea}The five prayers came from beside that Tree.{/idea}
old: The daily prayers are a routine to get through.
new: My five prayers are a gift brought back from the highest place.
try: Before your next prayer, take one breath and remember where it came from.

title: His sight did not wander or overreach.
subtitle: Discipline at the greatest moment
then: Ibn Abbas said his sight did not turn right or left. Ibn Kathir calls this {idea}a tremendous quality{/idea}: he did only what was commanded and {idea}did not ask beyond what he was given{/idea}, even surrounded by wonders.
now: You open your phone to answer one message and twenty minutes later you are deep in someone else's feed. {trap}Eyes that wander take the heart with them.{/trap} At the greatest sight ever shown, his eyes stayed where they were meant to be.
old: Looking around is harmless. My eyes go where they want.
new: A steady gaze is a form of obedience, even among wonders.
try: Open your phone today for one task, do it, and close it.

title: He saw some of his Lord's greatest signs.
subtitle: Signs that point to Allah's greatness
then: Ibn Kathir links this to the Night Journey verse: {idea}that We might show him of Our signs{/idea}. These were signs testifying to Allah's might and greatness. Some scholars took this verse to mean he saw signs, not Allah Himself.
now: A newborn's grip around your finger. A storm over the city. A scan on a doctor's screen. You saw a sign and moved on. {idea}A sign is meant to point past itself.{/idea}
old: Amazing things are just amazing things.
new: Every great sign is pointing me to its Lord.
try: Notice one thing today that amazes you and say SubhanAllah out loud.

title: Now look at al-Lat and al-Uzza.
subtitle: From the greatest signs to a stone and a tree
then: Right after the vision, the surah asks: have you considered these? Al-Lat was {trap}a white stone in Ta'if{/trap} with a house built around it. Al-Uzza was {trap}a tree at Nakhlah{/trap} revered by Quraysh. Ibn Jarir said both names were taken from Allah's names.
now: You would never bow to a stone. But you might check one app before you pray, or fear a boss's mood more than Allah. {trap}We all have things we quietly give too much weight to.{/trap} The question is for you too: have you considered them?
old: Idols are an old problem that has nothing to do with me.
new: Anything I give Allah's place to deserves a hard look.
try: Name one thing that pulls your attention before Allah does. Look at it honestly.

title: And Manat, the third one.
subtitle: Three famous idols, three tribes
then: Manat stood at Mushallal near Qudayd, between Makkah and Madinah. {trap}Aws, Khazraj and Khuza'ah revered it{/trap} and began their Hajj from beside it. Ibn Kathir says there were many idols in Arabia, but {idea}these three were named because they were the most famous{/idea}.
now: Every family has its sacred thing nobody questions: the way it has always been done, what the neighbors will say. {trap}The most famous habits are the hardest to look at.{/trap}
old: If everyone around me respects something, it must be fine.
new: Even the most famous thing can be just a name.
try: Pick one family habit you follow without thinking and ask whether it pleases Allah.

title: Sons for you, daughters for Him?
subtitle: They gave Allah what they disliked for themselves
then: The idolaters claimed the angels were Allah's daughters, while preferring sons for themselves. Ibn Kathir explains the question: {trap}do you choose female offspring for Allah and keep the males for yourselves?{/trap} Their own logic was turned back on them.
now: You keep the best for yourself and hand Allah the leftovers: the tired last prayer of the night, the coins at the bottom of your pocket. {trap}We give Him what we would not accept ourselves.{/trap}
old: Whatever I give Allah is fine, even if it is my leftovers.
new: If I would not accept it myself, why offer it to Him?
try: Give something today from what you like most, not what is left over.

title: That is a crooked division.
subtitle: Unfair even between people
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}if you split things like this between yourselves and other people, it would be unjust{/trap}. How then can you make that split between yourselves and Allah? The word means unfair, crooked.
now: You notice instantly when a sibling gets the bigger share of an inheritance. Your sense of fairness is sharp when it is about you. {idea}This verse asks you to use that same sharpness about what you give Allah.{/idea}
old: I notice unfairness only when it is done to me.
new: The fairness I demand from others, I owe in what I give Allah.
try: Think of one place you expect more from others than you give. Even it out today.

title: Only names you and your fathers invented.
subtitle: Guesswork and desire, while guidance has arrived
then: Ibn Kathir says they had {trap}no proof except trust in their forefathers{/trap}, plus a desire to lead and to keep their fathers honored. Meanwhile {idea}guidance had already come to them{/idea} through the Messengers.
now: Someone asks why you do something, and the only answer you have is: that is how my family does it, or everyone in my circle thinks so. {trap}A name and a habit are not proof.{/trap}
old: Our ways are right because our elders handed them down.
new: A name without proof is only a name, however old it is.
try: Ask yourself why you hold one belief today, and look for its proof.

title: Does a person get whatever he wishes?
subtitle: Wishing is not the same as earning
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}not everyone who claims to be guided is truly guided{/trap}, and not everyone gets what he wishes for himself. He cites the hadith: {idea}when one of you wishes, let him be careful what he wishes for{/idea}, for he does not know what of it will be written.
now: You tell yourself you will become a better person someday, you will pray properly after this busy season, after the wedding, after the exam. {trap}A wish is not a plan.{/trap}
old: I mean well, so it will work out for me.
new: Wishing for good is not the same as walking toward it.
try: Turn one good wish into one small step you take today.

title: Both lives belong to Allah.
subtitle: The last and the first, in one hand
then: After the question about wishes, the answer: {idea}all matters belong to Allah{/idea}, King of this world and the next. Ibn Kathir says whatever He wills occurs, and {idea}whatever He does not will never occurs{/idea}.
now: You plan your career, your house, your retirement, as if this life were yours to run and the next one far away. {idea}Both are in the same Hands.{/idea} The one who decides your payday decides your ending too.
old: This life is mine to run. The next one is far away.
new: This life and the next belong to the same Owner.
try: Add in sha Allah sincerely to one plan you make today.

title: Even angels intercede only with His permission.
subtitle: So what can a stone do?
then: The idolaters hoped their idols would intercede for them. Ibn Kathir reasons: {idea}if this is the case with angels who are close to Him{/idea}, how can anyone hope for the help of idols without His permission? He links it to the Throne Verse.
now: You look for the right contact, the cousin who knows someone, the person whose word will fix your problem. {trap}We trust connections.{/trap} Even the highest beings need Allah's leave. Go to Him first.
old: If I know the right person, my problem is solved.
new: No one can help me without Allah's leave, so I ask Him first.
try: Before you call anyone for help with a problem today, ask Allah first.
